text:
eli: Heads-up — users hit a weird failure when redwood-hsm-plugin binds a UNIX socket under /tmp on RHEL9 with SELinux Enforcing. The socket gets tmp_t and is blocked by redwood_t. I opened a docs PR with a recommended migration path + systemd override and an airgap note: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4622

sara: can you summarize the repro steps here so reviewers don't need to run it?

eli: short repro: start redwood-hsm-plugin configured to write /tmp/pkcs11.sock, set SELinux=Enforcing, ensure plugin runs as systemd service with PrivateTmp=yes. The plugin creates the socket in its PrivateTmp -> label tmp_t -> redwood process can't open it. audit.log shows AVC denials.

ivan: thanks. we should cover both RHEL/SELinux and Debian/Ubuntu AppArmor behavior. AppArmor won't relabel, but PrivateTmp still isolates /tmp; for AppArmor the fix is usually a persistent path under /var/lib and update apparmor profile to allow access.

eli: PR contains two suggested fixes: 1) preferred: use /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket + set SELinux fcontext and restorecon at install time; 2) fallback: disable PrivateTmp for that unit. I also added a tiny migration script for existing installs that checks for sockets in /tmp and moves them.

sara: paste the migration script snippet here so we can quick-check it in-thread?

eli: sure — here's the snippet in the PR (kept minimal for airgapped):

```bash
# migrate-hsm-socket.sh
set -euo pipefail
OLD=/tmp/pkcs11.sock
NEW_DIR=/var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket
NEW=$NEW_DIR/pkcs11.sock
if [ -S "$OLD" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$NEW_DIR"
  chmod 0755 "$NEW_DIR"
  if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    /sbin/restorecon -R "$NEW_DIR" || true
  fi
  systemctl stop redwood-hsm || true
  mv "$OLD" "$NEW"
  chown root:root "$NEW"
  systemctl start redwood-hsm || true
  echo "migrated $OLD -> $NEW"
else
  echo "no legacy socket found"
fi
```

ivan: add semanage suggestion for folks with policy tools: `semanage fcontext -a -t var_run_t '/var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket(/.*)?'` then `restorecon -Rv /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket`. If semanage not present, use `chcon -t var_run_t /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket` as a temporary step.

sara: wording suggestion: "Preferred: create persistent socket directory under /var/lib/redwood and ensure proper file context before starting the service. For air-gapped installs, run restorecon/semanage during the installer step; if not possible, document the chcon workaround and note it will not survive relabels." Keep it short in Troubleshooting bullets.

eli: also flagged CI link-check — my PR referenced an internal KB url that changed. docs-bot: replied with failing link to `https://kb.redwood.internal/selinux-sockets`

docs-bot: Link-check: fail in PR 4622 1 updated link suggested: https://kb.redwood.internal/selinux-sockets-v2 (internal) — mark for manual approval.

security-bot: please ensure the text does not tell users to run `setenforce 0` as a fix. Add explicit "do not disable SELinux system-wide" note.

ivan: added brief "do not disable SELinux" sentence in PR and included an explicit example of a systemd override unit that keeps PrivateTmp and uses RuntimeDirectory:

```ini
[Service]
PrivateTmp=yes
RuntimeDirectory=redwood-hsm
RuntimeDirectoryMode=0755
ExecStartPre=/bin/mkdir -p /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket
ExecStartPre=/usr/sbin/semanage fcontext -a -t var_run_t '/var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket(/.*)?' || true
ExecStartPre=/sbin/restorecon -R /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket || true
```

eli: I also added a short AppArmor note: for Ubuntu, add `/var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket/*` to the redwood-hsm profile and reload with `apparmor_parser -r /etc/apparmor.d/usr.bin.redwood-hsm`.

sara: great. final step: can someone from Security quick-approve the SELinux phrasing? cc @security-bot

security-bot: Reviewed. Phrase is safe; please remove the semanage example from the top-level quickstart (keep in advanced section) because semanage isn't available on minimal installs by default.

el i: done — moved semanage into Advanced > SELinux section. Will run copyedit and then request merge.

sara: thanks — i will run the airgap smoke instructions on a RHEL9 VM later today and report back. :thumbsup:

eli: thanks team. leaving this thread open for test results and any last-minute wording notes.
